bull.b: Exceptional Q1 growth (122% YoY) and multi‑period revenue gains indicate increasing commercial traction and product adoption. Sustained top‑line expansion improves the potential to scale fixed costs, enhance margins, and reduce reliance on external financing over a 2–6 month horizon if growth persists.

This extensive clinical footprint underpins international sales resilience and accelerates uptake once U.S. regulatory/technical issues are resolved.

Unless revenue scale or expense reductions occur, ongoing negative cash generation will necessitate dilution or other capital actions within the medium term.

This structural interruption reduces near‑term revenue visibility, complicates U.S. launch economics, and can slow clinical momentum until approvals and relaunch occur.

Nasdaq bid‑price noncompliance and leadership changes raise execution and investor confidence risk, while an increased authorized share count expands capacity for dilution. These structural governance and listing issues can constrain long‑term capital access and complicate strategic execution.
